findings.text: _count_parsed_bytes(len(data)) is invoked outside _PARSED_STREAM_LOCK at :3586, and _PARSED_STREAM_BYTES[0] += count (:3894) is a non-atomic read-modify-write consumed by take_parsed_stream_bytes (:3899) from the producer's poll accounting. Now that concurrent discovery threads reach the cache, the 'bytes parsed this poll' figure can under-count or be attributed across poll windows. Metrics only: no crash, no cache corruption. The line is unchanged by the reviewed commits, so this is a residual observation rather than a regression introduced here.

follow_ons: reckon/_backends.py:3894 _PARSED_STREAM_BYTES[0] += count is an unsynchronised read-modify-write now reachable from concurrent discovery threads; it feeds a poll-accounting metric only, so guard it with _PARSED_STREAM_LOCK (or document it as best-effort) if the counter must be exact. Outside this review node's write fence.

review_limitations: Read the target's three gained commits, its manifest, its evidence fragment and its base/after gate logs; independently reran tests/test_watch_stream_parse_is_cached.py at the reviewed head (3 passed) and independently reproduced the base race by overlaying the head test onto pre-fix source at 977aaf754 (1 failed, RuntimeError). Did not rerun the 222-test import suite or the CPU/warm-discovery measures.
This review attaches findings and scores only; it does not repair source, update the target manifest, merge commits, promote the target run or verify the merged primary head.

The call-site list is runtime reach read from the source, not a dynamic trace; the read-only contract of dialect.observe is evidenced by the per-iteration parity assertions in the concurrency test rather than by a source-only proof.
